checked_claims.note: The required target_interface_reference is present and correctly names ATT-0120, its source Y, the proper Borel–Moore image map, and the kernel T_Z. Its coverage claim nevertheless proves the stated unconditional Tate conclusion only assuming criterion (H), while GAP-0125-1 explicitly leaves (H) unresolved for strata of dimensions 9 through 16. Thus the interface reaches the correct target but does not prove the theorem.

Localization identifies T_Z with the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) in T. The degree and twist ledger is consistent: for dimension 21, H^{BM}_{16}=H^{26}(21), taking ordinary weight 26 to weight -16. This is proper pushforward, not an unrecorded Gysin shift.

On the coarse schemes actually used, Artin vanishing and Poincare duality give H^{BM}_{16}=0 for smooth affine strata of dimension at least 17; varieties of dimension below 8 contribute nothing, and the degree-16 top Borel–Moore group in dimension 8 is generated by fundamental classes of Tate type Q(8).

Repeated Borel–Moore localization removes smooth affine dense opens with vanishing degree-16 Borel–Moore homology and lowers the supporting closed subset to dimension at most 16. This uses exact localization, not spectral-sequence degeneration.

If the target image is supported on a closed subset of dimension at most 8, its degree-16 lowest-weight source is a sum of top-dimensional fundamental classes, so its image is a finite direct sum of Q(8). No upgrade from pure Tate to general algebraic or tautological generation is used.

The conditional implication from criterion (H) to the Tate conclusion follows by localization and semisimplicity of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures. At this pure one-type corner semisimplicity yields an actual Hodge-structure isomorphism, not merely equality after semisimplification.
The attempt accurately acknowledges that GAP-0125-1 prevents it from resolving the assigned theorem.

finding_candidates.statement: ATT-0125 supplies the genuine ATT-0120 source, map, and target subquotient, but its Tate conclusion for the named T_Z remains conditional on the explicitly undischarged GAP-0125-1, so it does not satisfy the unconditional target-interface coverage requirement.

proof_dependency_checks.note: Supplies the verified, atlas-independent closed support Y and the canonical kernel T_Z used by the candidate; the candidate does not substitute a family base, atlas, product model, or standalone Z.
The cited interface claims provide the named source, restriction kernel, proper target map, and weight bookkeeping required by target_interface_reference.
The ordinary/Borel–Moore dictionary and Tate twist are applied consistently: 2*21-16=26 and twisting by 21 changes weight 26 to -16.

The load-bearing localization and mixed-Hodge arguments are applied to separated finite-type coarse schemes. The dependency's exclusion of an unverified general Deligne–Mumford-stack formalism is therefore not crossed.
The candidate uses the required image-of-proper-pushforward interpretation of the supported target contribution, rather than identifying T_Z with an unsupported source group.
Applied to smooth affine coarse varieties in the support-lowering argument with the correct cohomological range.
Localization, strictness of weights, Poincare duality, top Borel–Moore classes, and semisimplicity are used with rational coefficients and the stated Tate twists.
Criterion (H) is not established for smooth strata of dimensions 9 through 16, yet it is required to deduce that the named T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8).

strongest_attack: The decisive attack is the target-interface coverage failure: although ATT-0125 supplies the required target_interface_reference and correctly reaches the named ATT-0120 kernel T_Z, its survival_or_tate_argument proves Tate type only conditional on criterion (H), which remains unresolved in dimensions 9 through 16. Consequently the unconditional theorem_statement is incomplete under FND-0189. The principal alternative attacks do not strengthen this to refutation: the load-bearing stack statements are reduced to rational coarse-scheme statements; all degrees and Tate twists match; no Gysin, Kunneth, spectral-sequence degeneration, graph-automorphism invariants/coinvariants, predicted-motive theorem, or stable-pair contribution is used; and semisimplicity yields an actual pure Hodge-structure decomposition. No non-Tate subquotient of the named T_Z is exhibited.
theorem_statement: Let T_Z be the canonical mixed-Hodge subquotient of T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) supplied by a verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum. Prove T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). A disproof must exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z through the verified target interface; non-Tate cohomology of an arbitrary family base, atlas, product model, standalone Z, or a source class whose target image is not proved nonzero is not a disproof. This theorem does not itself assemble the complementary target terms.
